useFor: Every action the reader takes, chosen by what it does and how loudly it should speak: a tone, an emphasis, three sizes, icon-only, in flight, in a line of text, and the floating button on a phone.

combineWith.how: In .page-head-actions for what applies to the whole page, end-aligned with the primary last.
In .card-foot for what decides the card's content, the primary last.
In .modal-footer, Cancel first and the confirming button last, its label repeating the action.
.btn--sm on the toolbar's trailing side, the primary last.
Ghost icon buttons in a .table--pin-end column keep a row's actions in reach on a wide table.
A data-tip on an icon-only button, and on a disabled one to say why it cannot be used.

notFor.text: Several actions on the same thing joined into one control
Picking one of a few options
More actions than a row has room for
A state or a category shown on a record

useFor: A few actions on the same thing joined into one control, and the split button that runs an action or opens a menu of its variants.

combineWith.how: The split button's caret carries data-menu-toggle and opens a .menu in the same .menu-anchor, the destructive variant last.
Every button in the group takes the same size class; the group itself carries none.
A field beside the group takes the matching size, so the row lines up.

notFor.text: Picking one of several options
Switching between views of one record
Paging through a list of results

useFor: The bar above a list or table: the search and filters on the leading side, the count and the list's actions on the trailing side, and the actions on a selection while there is one.

combineWith.how: Straight above the card that holds the table, outside it.
Under the page head on a list page; the page's own actions stay in the head.
The filters in force as removable chips in a row under the toolbar.
A search with a leading icon is an .input-group, and .toolbar-input goes on the group.
A view or a setting switched in place, among the filters.
The trailing actions that do not fit, behind one button at the end, the destructive one last.

notFor.text: Facets in a side panel with counts
A filter for each column of a table
Actions that apply to the whole page
Switching between views of one record

useFor: A short list of actions opened from a button, from a right-click, or from a value trigger that changes what it shows, with labels, separators, submenus and a filter.

combineWith.how: The caret of a split button opens the action's variants.
The selection's further actions at the end of the toolbar, the destructive one last naming how many it acts on.
The page head's actions fold into one menu behind .actions-more when the head is narrow.
The saved views, switched from a menu whose trigger names the view in use.
The column chooser is a menu of checkboxes behind a toolbar button.
The user widget's menu is the same .menu; there is no second panel style.

notFor.text: Content that explains something
Picking a value from a plain list
A few options that stay in view
The places in the app
Searching every command in the app

useFor: A small amount of content anchored to what opened it — why a row is pending, what a figure means, a glance at a record — opened by a click or by resting on it.

combineWith.how: A record's detail in the panel is .kv rows, whose gap keeps key and value apart in the shrink-to-fit box.
A small table in .popover--flush reaches the panel's rounded corners.
An AI label opens one that says which agent, how sure and what was there before, with the way back at its foot.
A count on a nav link opens one through data-popover without following the link.
A hover card on the button that opens a dialog previews what the dialog holds, and closes when it opens.

notFor.text: A list of actions
One line of help on a control
A question the reader must answer before going on
A record's whole detail beside the list

useFor: Rearranging what the app shows — a list's order, cards across lanes, tiles in a grid — by pointer, by a finger held still and by the keyboard, with each move reported for the app to make.

combineWith.how: A whole card can be the item, dragged from a handle in its head.
A zone inside a .sedna-scroll scrolls while a row is held near its edge.
data-drag-axis="slot" makes a day or a half hour a place an event is put.
A tree's rows reorder and move between branches with the same attributes.
Moving a column is a zone along the header row.
A dashboard's panels are the items of one grid zone.

notFor.text: Files dropped from the desktop
Choosing several rows to act on
